page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 2,832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and operates without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show strong compute and data processing capabilities across multiple vector and compression routines. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 41.5 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieved 18.1 GB/sec, placing in the top ten percent of tested environments. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 315.94 GB/sec, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 77,885.39 and an extended instructions score of 79,944.97. Memory subsystem performance demonstrated cached read throughput of 5,011.43 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 102.98 GB/sec. Redis SET operations measured 77.15 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 53.8 GB/sec.

With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance is structurally constrained for memory-heavy databases or large in-memory graphs, which require broader addressable capacity. However, pairing high-frequency AMD execution with 2,832 GB of bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-intensive workloads that require rapid scratch disk space without incurring auxiliary attached-storage costs. Optimal workloads include compute-heavy batch processing, continuous integration compilation tasks, Redis caching layers, web application serving, data extraction pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based inference models.
description: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v7 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. It provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs from 24 physical cores alongside 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The host features 2,832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and omits discrete GPU hardware. Performance metrics demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compression throughput, highlighted by gzip speeds of 41.5 GB/sec, complemented by a multi-core PassMark CPU score of 77,885.39 and Redis throughput exceeding 77 million operations per second. Because memory per core is restricted relative to conventional general-purpose sizes, the configuration provides efficient resource balancing for tasks requiring fast compute and ample local scratch disk rather than large working memory. Primary workload targets include continuous integration pipelines, web serving, compressed data manipulation, caching nodes, and batch transformation workloads.
